name: The Big Duck Boat Tours
summary: Wildlife tours in rigid inflatable boats from the Granite Island Causeway at Victor Harbor and from St Vincent Marina at Wirrina Cove, on the Fleurieu Peninsula. Tours visit seal and sea lion colonies on the islands and coast of the Encounter Marine Park, with dolphins and, from June to September, whales. Private charters are available on both boats.
standouts: Gold in the Ecotourism category at the 2023 and 2024 South Australian Tourism Awards
Licensed whale watching vessel that keeps 300 metres from whales
Supports monthly Dolphin Watch surveys and runs its own sea lion monitoring program

contact.address: Main Wharf, Goolwa, South Australia (reservations office, open 7 days)

trips.title: Seal Island Tour
trips.summary: A 45 minute boat tour from the Granite Island Causeway at Victor Harbor. The boat passes Granite Island and its rock formations, then continues to Seal Island, home to fur seals, sea lions and seabirds. The crew talks about the history of the area, and routes change with the weather and where the wildlife is.
highlights: Passes Granite Island and its rock formations
Seal Island, home to fur seals, sea lions and seabirds
Local history from the crew
Family ticket available
trips.season: Year round (Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday, plus extra departure days through winter and school holidays)
trips.departsFrom: Granite Island Causeway, Victor Harbor (boat landing about 300m along the causeway)
includes: Commentary from the skipper and crew
bring: Warm clothing: it is often about 10 degrees cooler on the ocean than on land, even in summer
Camera or binoculars if you like (salt spray can reach the boat)
Eat and drink before or after the tour, as the ride can be bumpy and take on spray
If you are prone to sea sickness, a ginger tablet or travel-sickness medication at least 1 hour before
trips.requirements: Minimum age 2 years; children 2 to 15 must be accompanied by at least one adult. Not suitable for pregnant women. The front 5 rows have seat belts and the most motion; passengers there must be able to sit with their feet firmly on the floor, and there is a height restriction of 1500mm for the forward section. Not wheelchair accessible; passengers need to manage steps to board. No pets except registered guide dogs. Every passenger signs a digital waiver before boarding (a parent or guardian signs for under 18s).
trips.checkNotes: Tour page says prices are valid to 31 March 2027 and the tour departs 12:45pm (usually). Operating days are Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday, plus extra days in winter and school holidays. Age, height, pregnancy, access, waiver and what-to-bring details come from the FAQ, Accessibility and Booking Terms pages, which cover both Victor Harbor tours. Booking terms say a minimum of 2 passengers per tour and 6 passengers in a day are needed for tours to run. The page also says wildlife sightings are not guaranteed; not repeated here. The tour page banner photo (seal-2870893_1920.jpg) has a stock-style file name and was not used.

trips.title: Southern Ocean Adventure
trips.summary: A 90 minute tour from Victor Harbor past Granite Island and Seal Rock to West Island, where seals, sea lions and seabirds gather. The route continues along the cliffs at Kings Beach and Waitpinga before returning to the Granite Island Causeway. From June to September the same tour also looks for whales.
highlights: Route passes Granite Island, Seal Rock and West Island
Fur seals, sea lions and seabirds on the islands
Cliffs at Kings Beach and Waitpinga
Whale watching on the same tour from June to September

trips.title: Winter Whale Watching
trips.summary: A June to September version of the 90 minute Southern Ocean Adventure that looks for southern right and humpback whales around Encounter Bay. The vessel is a licensed whale watching vessel and stays at least 300 metres from whales. When whales are not in the area, the tour runs as a wildlife tour of dolphins, seals, sea lions and birds.

trips.title: Sea Wirrina Tour
trips.summary: A 75 minute tour from St Vincent Marina at Wirrina Cove along the Fleurieu Peninsula coast, past Second Valley and Rapid Bay. It visits a fur seal colony, and guests look out for white-bellied sea eagles overhead. The coastline is more sheltered than at Victor Harbor, so there is no minimum age and the tour suits the whole family.
highlights: Coastline past Second Valley and Rapid Bay
Fur seal colony
Look out for white-bellied sea eagles overhead
No age restrictions; suitable for pregnant women
trips.season: October to April (Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday)

trips.title: Private Charters
trips.summary: Two Naiad rigid inflatable boats can be chartered by groups at a flat rate: Pungari at Victor Harbor and Kondoli at Wirrina Cove. Each carries up to 40 passengers and the price is the same for any number of people. Charters are run for school and education groups, research groups, coach tours and private events.
highlights: Pungari at Victor Harbor and Kondoli at Wirrina Cove
Flat rate for up to 40 passengers
90 minute charters on any day of the week
Schools, citizen science, coach groups and special events

checkNotes: Notices on the site: (1) The Whale Log post of 17 September 2026 calls it the unofficial end of the 2026 whale season, so Winter Whale Watching is out of season as of mid October 2026; the other tours are described as running year round (Victor Harbor) or October to April (Sea Wirrina). (2) A bird flu page and a FAQ entry say tours are operating as normal. (3) A Harmful Algal Bloom page says the ocean tours have not been impacted; it refers to events from 2025 and may be out of date. Booking: every trip with a link uses a per-trip Rezdy link found on the operator's own page (shop alias thebigduck). Private Charters are sold by enquiry only. Not treated as trips: the 'Tour Menu' link on the Contact page (thebigduck.rezdy.com/catalog/180455/tour-menu), the BOOK NOW and Tour Calendar menu links (thebigduck.rezdy.com and /productsCalendar/180455), and the Book Now page (/bookyourcruisehere), which embeds the whole booking shop in a frame. Gift vouchers are sold through an embedded Rezdy gift card catalog on the Buy Vouchers page (thebigduck.rezdy.com/catalog/190584/gift-cards). No Rezdy page was opened. Spirit of the Coorong (spiritofthecoorong.com.au) is a sister brand run by the same director with Coorong National Park tours; it is a separate site and was not included. Earlier Murray Mouth tours appear only in old YouTube video titles and are not described on the site. Prices on the Victor Harbor and Sea Wirrina tour pages are stated as valid to 31 March 2027. Cancellation terms (Booking Terms): no refund if cancelled less than 24 hours before departure or for late arrivals; full refund or credit if cancelled more than 24 hours before; an alternate date or full refund if the operator cancels (for example weather). The Environment page says an optional $5 donation to Dolphin Watch and an optional $2 carbon offset contribution are offered during online booking; they are not on the tour pages and were not entered as price options. Contact: the Contact page shows phone (08) 8555 2203, bookings@thebigduck.com.au and an office on the Main Wharf in Goolwa. The page's hidden site data lists a different phone (0405125312) and a Victor Harbor Tramway address; those are not shown to visitors and were not used. The site makes strong claims that were not repeated: carbon negative and climate positive, a full offset of operational emissions, past whale counts, and wildlife sighting language. The 2023 and 2024 award wording is from the Environment page text; award badges on the home page also show a 2025 Gold Ecotourism award and a Hall of Fame logo, which the page text does not explain, so they were not used.
